why: Learn AR with SPECS hackathon: fills your own empty venue with a life-size ghost crowd at a density you choose, so stewards can stand inside the 5-people-per-square-metre danger line. Video (H1h7XHV2v-U) is a Lens Studio preview only.

name: Spectacles Community Challenge #17 winners (Aadarsh Pandey — After Hello; Natasha Gubernov — Pottery AR; Daria LASTXLR — Wondermarks; Steven Wolpe — Jurnee; Kavin Kumar — Spatial Mapper)
why: Announced 2026-11-13: ASL-to-captions conversation aid for two people, two-handed clay throwing with a kiln and a shelf you can smash pots from, landmarks placed on a world map, an AR journal with a butterfly guide, and tracing a real projector's light outline for projection mapping. No public video found for any of them; check the creators' X, LinkedIn and r/Spectacles.

name: Amir Mohideen Basheer Khan — SpecsGrip
why: Spectacles Community Challenge #17 (Open Source, 1st): Specs hand tracking mirrors all 20 joints of your hand onto a Tesollo Delto DG-5F robot hand in real time. The only video is an mp4 in the GitHub README (user-attachments/assets/089905e0-afa3-4d06-90e4-105c6f981827, checks ok) that was not watched in this round; add if it shows the real robot hand.

name: Firechant — Puttscape
why: Multiplayer mini golf for XREAL AURA (Android XR) with hand-tracked putting, a course generated from your room and a venue mode run from a Pixel Fold. The 8-minute devlog (Twiu_hiEY4U) mixes talking head and AI-generated cutscenes; look for a short see-through gameplay clip before adding.

name: AnySketch Neo (Meta Quest 3 prototype)
why: Meta VR Start 2026 entry: pin a line-art stencil on your real desk or wall in passthrough and trace it with a real pencil on real paper; any photo becomes a stencil. Real headset footage, but the video (bAr1OsbbcWQ) fails check_video (embedding disabled, HTTP 401).

name: Sushant Srikrish — Chartrise
why: Meta VR Start 2026 entry: a strategy game laid flat on the real desk like a giant tablet, so every virtual button has a solid surface under the finger; the battle can rise into a hologram or be entered at full scale. Real Quest 3 footage (Bobl1g3LGKI); a good passive-haptics example if a further Quest round is wanted.

name: Matthew Neuffer — Sneak-A-Snack
why: Meta VR Start 2026 entry: a two-player camp game where hand shadows on a tent wall are the only way to communicate which snacks to grab. Fully VR rather than mixed reality (CUzi74dLO7Q), but a strong hand-shadow-as-language idea next to the existing hand-shadow lead.

name: Clarke Plumo Dev — Soothing Bots
why: Meta VR Start 2026 entry: sixteen floating robot heads sing a story song in mixed reality, each voice coming from its own head; wake them with a pinch, carry them around the room, and they answer a peace sign, a wave or a high five (ZVg9R9TkKnc). Not viewed frame by frame in this round.

name: Tenstud (Argi Tendo) — THROUGH
why: Meta VR Start 2026 entry: open a portal in your wall onto a fading garden, rescue sprouts and guide rain and light with bare hands until giant blooms grow into your own room (_xMdysRSQIE, actual gameplay according to the description). Check the footage before adding.

name: Natasha Gubernov — ArtGuide
why: Spectacles Community Challenge #16 (New Lens, 2nd): projects composition guides, reference images, AI feedback and on-demand 3D still lifes onto the artist's real paper or canvas. Lenslist spotlight 2026-11-04. No public video found; try her X or LinkedIn.

name: Shahwali Shayan — Plane Spotter
why: Spectacles Community Challenge #16 (New Lens, 1st): Heathrow Airport as a live tabletop model driven by real flight data, with tappable aircraft cards. No public video found.

name: Baruch Geuze — OpenBand
why: Spectacles Community Challenge #16 (Open Source, 1st): control Spectacles from a smartwatch with pinch and forearm gestures plus haptic feedback. Repo public; no video found (GitHub API blocked during this round).

name: Elsa Farrokhzadeh (urbanpeppermint) — Spatial AI DJ
why: Spectacles Community Challenge #16 (Open Source, 3rd): an AI-generated mix you shape by dragging pucks across four decks in 3D space. Has a YouTube channel (@urbanpeppermint) but no video of this Lens yet.

name: Tim Van Leemput — ParaKo
why: Meta VR Start 2026 entry: a tiny parasite takes root in your hand in mixed reality; feed it, catch flies with a sway of the hand, and it grows gifts that change what your hands can do. Only a 57 s trailer so far (_9iRUYeJVoE); look for gameplay.

name: Abhimanyu R B — Perihelion
why: Meta VR Start 2026 WebXR puzzle: pinch and slingshot a comet, plant gravity wells in the air, or put a real cup on your desk and it bends the comet too. Video (Ds5Jt9tzgnA) appears to be emulator footage; check for a real-desk recording.

name: yi yu — Foldlings
why: Meta VR Start 2026 WebXR origami: fold a virtual sheet with bare hands until it becomes a creature that settles on a real surface in your room. Open source (github.com/yy5652-hash/foldlings), but the video (RX2S5l6ZVmA) mixes web-build captures with Blender renders.

name: Frameless Labs — The Winner Takes It All
